title: Hitchcock and suspense
subject: art
description: **Alfred Hitchcock** invents modern suspense: giving the audience information that the characters do not have. With *Psychology*, *Vertigo* or *The Rear Window*, he manipulates our gaze.

hero.hook: The real suspense doesn't surprise: it lets you see the bomb under the table.

blocks.text: **Alfred Hitchcock** (1899-1980) is nicknamed the “master of suspense”. In more than fifty films, he transformed the thriller into the art of manipulation. *Psychology*, *Vertigo*, *The Rear Window*: each time, the camera does not just tell a story. She plays with our nerves.
His favorite subject is not crime. It’s the look: guilt, obsession, voyeurism. Hitchcock films the viewer as much as the characters.

In **1966**, Hitchcock explains his method to , a French critic and then filmmaker. The **surprise**, he says, is a bomb that explodes without warning: a brief shock. The **suspense** is showing the audience the bomb while the characters ignore it. The tension lasts. We become complicit, and powerless. [[François Truffaut]]

blocks.caption: Hitchcock: a face, a silhouette, a global brand of thrill.

blocks.text: To advance the plot, he often uses a [[The MacGuffin]]: an object or secret that motivates the characters, but whose exact nature matters little. The important thing is the hunt.
This information asymmetry is its grammar. As soon as we know more than the hero, we fear for him.

In **1948**, with *The Rope*, Hitchcock simulates a unique : the film seems to be shot in one go. The reels only last ten minutes, so he hides the cuts behind a back or a dark piece of furniture. The effect is suffocating: we remain locked up with the murderers. [[sequence shot]]

blocks.caption: Vertigo: vertigo filmed as a distortion of space.

blocks.text: In **1958**, for *Vertigo*, he invented the [[Dolly Zoom]]: the camera moves back while the zoom advances (or vice versa). Space is distorted. We no longer see the vertigo. We feel it.

In *The Rear Window* (**1954**), a photographer with a broken leg spies on his neighbors. He is the spectator's double in the dark. Hitchcock uses : we see exactly what the hero sees, nothing more. [[Subjective camera (point of view shot)]]

This identification is moral as well as visual. We look for clues, but we also share the guilt of looking at what doesn't concern us. Hitchcock mixes thriller and : buried fears, forbidden desires, double identities. [[psychoanalysis]]

sections.title: A brand, a music, a heritage

blocks.text: Hitchcock transformed his name into a brand, leading to his television series *Alfred Hitchcock Presents*. For *Psychology*, he prohibits entry after the start of the session: the secret becomes an event. His collaboration with composer  links music and  to quicken the audience's pulse. [[Bernard Herrmann]] [[assembly]]
Hitchcock codified modern suspense: informing the viewer, directing their gaze, and transforming fear into controlled pleasure. Decades later, the thriller still owes its grammar to him.
